one_liner: Ramp has a broad REST Developer API with OAuth2 (client credentials and authorization code), a sandbox, and an official MCP server. Production publishing to other businesses goes through Ramp review.
auth_notes: Supports Client Credentials and Authorization Code with refresh tokens. The token endpoint uses HTTP Basic with client_id:client_secret, but that is only for the token exchange, so the method is classed as OAuth2.
access_notes: Any Ramp account admin can create a developer app and get sandbox credentials. The API agreement says access requires a request for Ramp review. Publishing an app to other Ramp businesses uses the Developer console and partner program. Some scopes need a support ticket, and some endpoints need a plan feature.
blocker_notes: Multi-user OAuth for other Ramp businesses requires publishing through the Developer console, which is subject to Ramp's review. Credentials also need a Ramp account with admin access.

evidence.quote: Currently Ramp supports two grant types -- Client Credentials and Authorization Code.
Ramp authenticates this `/developer/v1/token` request with HTTP Basic Auth: base64-encode `client_id:client_secret` and send it in the `Authorization` header.
To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.
To receive access to the Ramp APIs in a sandbox or production environment, you must submit a request for Ramp review.
Partners can work with real-time spend data, approval workflows, user provisioning and spend controls, virtual cards, vendor payouts, and more.
Ramp hosts an official remote server at `https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp` (with a sample-data variant at `https://demo-mcp.ramp.com/mcp`).
A Model Context Protocol server for retrieving and analyzing data or running tasks for [Ramp](https://ramp.com) using [Developer API]
